_comment: CONFIRMED 2026-11-16 (local, read-only): the 13 input-signal names were read from gatekeeper.wasm itself via getInputSignalSize (calibrated: unknown names return 0), and a fullProve+verify against the real vk.json succeeds for VALID+APPROVE and for each trap+REJECT, while wrong decisions assert-fail at GatekeeperEvaluation line 102. Supersedes input-mapping.json.example (whose snake_case names and proof_tx signal do not exist in this circuit).

_encoding.decision: APPROVE=1, REJECT=0. The circuit asserts decision == (all in-circuit conditions pass). PROOF_REUSED has no in-circuit signal (no proof_tx input): proving a REJECT for it assert-fails by design — the server must respond without a proof (docs: REUSED tasks are excluded from the proof bonus).
_encoding.public_signals_order: [commitment, proofVkHash, registeredVkHash, minimum, publicBalance, expiryBlock, currentBlock, conditionRecipient, recipient, amount, maxTransfer, decision, taskId] — commitment is circuit-derived from salt+taskId
_encoding.registeredVkHash: blake2b-256 of the 32 raw vk bytes, decimal field element (mod p). Any consistent hash verifies cryptographically (keccak also verified); blake2b matches this repo's zkVerify hashing (src/onchain.js). Platform-side convention still unconfirmed — worst case the proof counts as invalid (-2, same as no proof).
_encoding.taskId: blake2b-256 of the task_id UTF-8 string, decimal field element (mod p). Unconstrained for validity (taskId=1 also verifies); blake2b chosen for consistency.
